text.p: The Oakland Athletics re-acquired Jose Canseco, the slugging outfielder and designated hitter from the Boston Red Sox, in exchange for pitcher John Wasdin on Monday.

A spokesperson from the Athletics said the deal was contingent upon both players passing physicals. The teams had been discussing a trade for weeks, but Oakland originally balked at giving Wasdin to the Red Sox.
"The deal was consummated this morning when Canseco passed a physical," said Athletics assistant general manager Bill Beane.
"We reluctantly give up a player of John Wasdin's potential," added Beane. "He is a player from whom we expect great things in the major leagues.

"But with his recent back surgery, we expect Jose to come back as great as ever. People forget he is only 32 years old. It's had an immediate impact from the corporate sales standpoint. Today was our greatest ticket sales day of the entire winter."

For Oakland the trade represents little risk, especially after the Red Sox agreed to pick up a large portion of Canseco's $4.5 million salary. Canseco's 1997 contract also calls for $1.275 million in incentive payments.

"I think I'm a much better player, a much better hitter actually," Canseco said when asked about how he has matured since his last stint in Oakland. "With Jose on the field and Jose off the field, there has been some improvement. I think if (Mark) McGwire and I can stay healthy all year, if we can average 150 to 160 games, I think that we are definitely going to win our division."

Canseco has been on the disabled list several times since being acquired from the Texas Rangers after the 1994 season. He had surgery to repair a ruptured disc in early August and did not return to the lineup until mid-September.
Used primarily as a designated hitter, Canseco batted .289 with 28 homers and 82 RBI last season. He demanded to be traded following the firing of manager Kevin Kennedy.

Canseco began his career with Oakland in 1985 and was the American League MVP with the Athletics in 1988, when he became the only player in major-league history to hit 40 homers and steal 40 bases in the same season.
The trade reunites him with fellow "Bash Brother" McGwire, who led the majors with 52 homers last season. The duo powered Oakland to the 1989 World Series title.
Wasdin, a 24-year-old, posted an 8-7 record with a 5.96 ERA in 25 games this season, including 21 starts.
